skill1: ■ Activates when landing a Full Charge attack during Full Burst. Affects the target. Taunts for 5 sec.
skill2: ■ Activates when hitting a target's Parts for 5 time(s). Affects all allies. Damage to Parts ▲ 10.05% for 5 sec.
burst: ■ Activates when Muscle Up is at max stacks. Affects self. Damage Taken ▼ 20.06% for 10 sec.

caveats: ⚑ CADENCE (mandatory for a charge weapon): pullsPerSec / reloadFrames 129 / chargeFrames 60 are datamined-unreliable, and whether this RL AUTOFIRES (noBoltRecovery) vs takes the measured 22-frame bolt gap is a ~15-20% shot-count swing not derivable from kit text. Engine default (bolt gap ON) shipped unmeasured; do not set noBoltRecovery without footage.

⚑ MUSCLE UP STEADY STATE: 3.04% Max HP per full charge, cap 5, 2 sec duration. At the RL charge cycle implied by chargeFrames 60 + bolt gap + a 6-round magazine (~1.3-1.5 s/shot), only ~1-2 stacks are ever concurrently live, so the cap is effectively unreachable outside a charge-speed buff. Offensively inert today (this kit carries no atkOfMaxHpPct consumer); kept for a future HP scaler and because the burst's max-stack clause reads it.

⚑ SKILL1 TRIGGER MAPPING: 'performing a Full Charge attack' is authored as shotFired, which assumes every RL trigger pull resolves as a full charge. If partial-charge pulls exist, the stack rate is overstated (damage-neutral while the granted stat is inert).

SKILL2 SKIPPED, NOT DROPPED: the Damage-to-Parts buff is doubly inert at scope lock — partsDamagePct is inert in v1 and the boss is partless, so the parts-hit trigger never fires. Modeling it on a hitCount:5 proxy would make it fire when the real condition cannot, a trigger-identity error; the line is recorded verbatim in unmodeled instead. Magnitude if it is ever wired: 10.05% partsDamagePct to all allies, 5 sec, on 5 parts hits.

The burst's Damage Taken ▼ 20.06% is a SELF damage-reduction, not the enemy-facing damageTakenPct debuff. No HP pool is modeled at scope lock, so it has no channel; it is not the team-benefiting 'Damage Taken ▲' shape.
override.note: PARSER BASELINE (HYPOTHESIS — NOT a validated model). Every ⚑ below is an UNMEASURED estimate; hand-tune + record against a real fight before trusting any number. Rumani (rumani) is an RL/Fire/Defender/Burst I whose ONLY offensive channel in this kit is the burst's team-wide Normal Attack Damage Multiplier ▲ 10.05% for 10 sec — everything else is Max HP, taunt, parts, or self damage-reduction. Burst lines carry no activation clause and grant a self mode plus a team buff, so they are keyed burstCast (fires only on rotations this unit bursts), not fullBurstEnter. The two Max HP grants use targetMaxHpPct ('Max HP ▲ X%' = % of the target's own Max HP) and are offensively inert for this unit — no atkOfMaxHpPct consumer in kit — but are kept per the never-skip-HP rule as a future scaler feed. No function-damage riders, DoTs, weapon swaps, or shot-count modifiers appear anywhere in the kit, so there is no noFb decision to make and no reload/ammo/fire-rate line to audit.

flags.field: cadence tuple (base weapon: pullsPerSec / reloadFrames 129 / chargeFrames 60 / bolt recovery)
flags.estimate: Ship the datamined tuple with the engine-default 22-frame bolt-recovery gap ON (RL default). Implied charge cycle ~1.3-1.5 s/shot, 6-round magazine, ~2.15 s reload.
flags.reasoning: Datamined rate_of_fire and reloadFrames are known-unreliable fields, and the autofire-vs-bolt-gap question is a documented ~15-20% shot-count swing (Liberalio root case) that is NOT visible in kit text. Setting noBoltRecovery unmeasured would be fudge-over-measured. RL rates are frame-exact per the 2026-07-23 quantization census (60/90/120/180/300 rpm all divide 60 cleanly), so quantization is not the risk here — autofire is.
flags.recipe: Focus recording of rumani: two frames 0.5 s apart in a no-reload window, read the ammo counter to get pulls/s directly; repeat in a second range band to confirm it is the weapon's rate and not an artifact. Separately time a reload (last shot to full counter) against the datamined 129 frames. If the counter shows no inter-shot recovery gap, set charFixes.noBoltRecovery:true.

flags.field: override.skill1[0].effects[0] — Muscle Up steady-state stack level
flags.estimate: ~1-2 concurrent stacks (~3-6% Max HP), not the 5-stack cap.
flags.reasoning: Stack/currency steady-state is an ALWAYS-⚑ field. Here the trajectory is partially derivable: 2 sec duration against a full-charge cycle of ~1.3-1.5 s admits only ~1-2 live stacks, so the cap is unreachable without external charge-speed support. Encoded faithfully (per-shot trigger + maxStacks 5 + durationSec 2) rather than as a fixed average, so the engine derives the real level from the actual cadence — which makes this flag DOWNSTREAM of the cadence ⚑ above. Damage impact today is zero (targetMaxHpPct has no consumer in this kit).
flags.recipe: Resolve the cadence ⚑ first; the stack level then falls out of the shot interval. To verify directly, DBG_BUFFS on a solo run and count concurrent Muscle Up stacks. In-game confirmation would be the stack pip count on her buff icon during sustained fire, and again inside a charge-speed buff window.

flags.estimate: shotFired (every trigger pull treated as a Full Charge attack).
flags.reasoning: The kit says 'performing a Full Charge attack' but TriggerDef has no full-charge trigger; chargeCounter is a cycling PHASE counter (effects[P] per phase), which mis-fits a single unconditional per-charge effect. For an RL with chargeFrames 60 the engine's pulls are full-charge shots, so shotFired is the faithful mapping. If partial-charge pulls are possible the stack rate is overstated.
flags.recipe: Footage check: does rumani ever fire before the charge bar fills? If yes, the trigger needs a full-charge gate and shotFired over-counts. Zero damage consequence while targetMaxHpPct stays inert — re-check before any HP-scaling consumer is added to her kit.

flags.estimate: value 10.05 read as a multiplicative scale on the normal-attack multiplier (x1.1005), team-wide, 10 sec from burst cast.
flags.reasoning: 'Normal Attack Damage Multiplier ▲' maps to normalAttackPct ('scales the normal attack multiplier'), which is the multiplier-scaling stat rather than an additive Damage-Up entry. This is the entire offensive output of the kit, so the bucket choice is load-bearing: if the line actually belongs in the additive Damage Up bucket (attackDamagePct) it would be diluted by other support buffs instead of scaling cleanly, and the team delta would differ.
flags.recipe: Popup A/B on a teammate with a clean normal-attack value: record one magazine outside rumani's burst window and one inside, same range band and no other buff changing state. A clean x1.1005 on the normal-attack popups confirms the multiplier reading; a smaller-than-10.05% lift in a buff-heavy team indicates additive-bucket dilution instead.

flags.field: override.unmodeled.skill2 — Damage to Parts ▲ 10.05% (all allies, 5 sec, on 5 parts hits)
flags.estimate: Zero contribution at scope lock; if parts modeling ever lands, author as allies + partsDamagePct 10.05 + durationSec 5 behind a real parts-hit trigger.
flags.reasoning: Both halves are inert on a partless boss: partsDamagePct is documented parsed-but-inert in v1, and the parts-hit trigger has no representation. Skipping is strictly safer than a hitCount:5 proxy, which would latently over-credit the moment partsDamagePct is wired live. Recorded verbatim rather than dropped.
flags.recipe: No measurement can settle this at scope lock — the boss has no parts. Revisit only if the sim gains destructible-part modeling and a multi-part boss; at that point the trigger needs a parts-hit primitive in TriggerDef, not a hit-count approximation.
